caveats: A detection near a box is not evidence that the box burned: a VIIRS pixel locates a thermal anomaly, not a burn perimeter. No class is suggested and no box is ranked.
Distance is to the box polygon in a local metre plane; a detection inside the box is 0. Bands are inclusive at 375, 750 and 1500 m.
Chip dates are read from the dated SWIR filenames in data/labels/imagery, so adding a file adds a date. The detection store's acq_date is already a WIT local day and is not shifted.

The per-chip distance is the nearest later detection. The box table uses the latest detection within 375 m, so the chips list describes the last near thermal anomaly; the literal nearest detection is stored beside it. Ties use the latest date, then the nearest distance.
Every box has an entry for every chip date. A box with no later detection anywhere in the record gets null distances and dates.
Free-text notes are incidental free text, not a general record of which chip a box was judged on. The committed labels carry far more notes than the 23 in the task text, and many now mention a date.
This is a lookup table for the owner's eye; it does not decide whether the 17 September sharpening is ground change or reconstruction.

The committed GeoPackage carries 71 notes across 142 boxes, not the 23 in the task text. They are free text, and many mention a date; they are not a general register of the chip each box was judged on.

parameters.chips_list: the table lists chips strictly before the latest detection within 375 m; the nearest-detection list is stored beside it
parameters.date_calendar: acq_date is WIT and is not shifted; chips are WIT days
parameters.distance_definition: distance to the box polygon in a local metre plane; inside = 0
parameters.later_than_chip: strictly greater than the chip date
parameters.latest_tie_break: nearest distance among detections on the latest date
parameters.nearest_tie_break: latest acq_date among equal minimum distance
